1: // Onion-Layered Relay — Tor-like onion routing for hop anonymity
2: //
3: // Each layer reveals only the next hop to relays, protecting both
4: // origin and destination from intermediate nodes.
5: 
6: use chacha20poly1305::aead::{Aead, KeyInit, Payload};
7: use chacha20poly1305::XChaCha20Poly1305;
8: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
9: use thiserror::Error;
10: use x25519_dalek::{EphemeralSecret, PublicKey};
11: 
12: use crate::crypto::pq::hybrid::{hybrid_decapsulate, hybrid_encapsulate, HybridCiphertext};
13: use crate::identity::keys::PublicKeyBundle;
14: 
15: /// Maximum number of hops in an onion circuit
16: pub const MAX_ONION_HOPS: usize = 5;
17: 
18: /// Size of X25519 public key (bytes)
19: const X25519_KEY_SIZE: usize = 32;
20: 
21: /// Size of XChaCha20-Poly1305 nonce (bytes)
22: const XCHACHA_NONCE_SIZE: usize = 24;
23: 
24: /// Size of Poly1305 authentication tag (bytes). Reserved constant for onion-layer size calculations; no current caller outside this module.
25: #[allow(dead_code)]
26: const POLY1305_TAG_SIZE: usize = 16;
27: 
28: /// Classical (v1) onion layer format - X25519 only
29: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
30: pub struct ClassicalOnionLayer {
31:     /// Ephemeral X25519 public key (32 bytes)
32:     pub ephemeral_pk: Vec<u8>,
33:     /// XChaCha20-Poly1305 encrypted routing info (contains next hop + nonce + tag)
34:     pub encrypted_routing_info: Vec<u8>,
35:     /// XChaCha20-Poly1305 encrypted remaining layers or payload
36:     pub encrypted_payload: Vec<u8>,
37: }
38: 
39: /// Hybrid (v2) onion layer format - X25519 + ML-KEM-768
40: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
41: pub struct HybridOnionLayer {
42:     /// Hybrid KEM ciphertext containing X25519 ephemeral and ML-KEM ciphertext
43:     pub hybrid_ct: HybridCiphertext,
44:     /// True if this is the innermost (destination) layer, in which case
45:     /// `payload` decrypts directly to the plaintext message. False for a
46:     /// relay layer, in which case `payload` decrypts to
47:     /// `(bool is_next_hybrid, next_hop_info) ++ remaining_layers`.
48:     /// Unlike ClassicalOnionLayer (which signals this via an empty
49:     /// encrypted_routing_info field), hybrid layers have no separate
50:     /// routing-info ciphertext, so this flag is the explicit equivalent --
51:     /// a relay learns this the moment it decrypts its own layer regardless,
52:     /// so storing it in cleartext here reveals nothing it wouldn't already
53:     /// determine on decrypt.
54:     pub is_destination: bool,
55:     /// XChaCha20-Poly1305 encrypted payload (next hop info + remaining layers,
56:     /// or the plaintext message if `is_destination`)
57:     pub payload: Vec<u8>,
58: }
59: 
60: /// Type of hop in the onion path

62: pub enum HopAddress {
63:     /// Classical hop using only X25519
64:     Classical([u8; X25519_KEY_SIZE]),
65:     /// Hybrid hop using X25519 + ML-KEM-768
66:     Hybrid(PublicKeyBundle),
67: }

75:         }
76:     }

78:     /// Check if this hop supports hybrid (PQ) encryption

1: //! Routing Decision Engine — Unified Layer Integration
2: //!
3: //! Combines all three routing layers (Local, Neighborhood, Global) to make optimal routing
4: //! decisions for every message. Implements mycorrhizal network principles: try direct paths
5: //! first, then nearby relays, then distant routes, and finally store-and-carry.
6: //!
7: //! Decision algorithm for every message:
8: //! 1. **Layer 1 (Mycelium)**: Check local cell for direct peer
9: //! 2. **Layer 2 (Rhizomorphs)**: Check neighborhood gateways if local misses
10: //! 3. **Layer 3 (CMN)**: Check global routes if neighborhood misses
11: //! 4. **Store-and-Carry**: No known route — hold until one appears or request discovery
12: 
13: use super::global::GlobalRoutes;
14: use super::local::{LocalCell, PeerId, TransportType};
15: use super::neighborhood::NeighborhoodTable;
16: 
17: /// Where to send a message next
18: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
19: pub enum NextHop {
20:     /// Deliver directly to a local peer
21:     Direct {
22:         peer_id: PeerId,
23:         transport: TransportType,
24:     },
25:     /// Forward through a gateway peer (Layer 2 path)
26:     Gateway {
27:         gateway_id: PeerId,
28:         transport: TransportType,
29:         hops_remaining: u8,
30:     },
31:     /// Forward through a global route (Layer 3 path)
32:     GlobalRoute { next_hop_id: PeerId, total_hops: u8 },
33:     /// Store and wait — no route known, carry until one appears
34:     StoreAndCarry,
35:     /// Broadcast route request — ask the network "who can reach this?"
36:     RouteDiscovery { hint: [u8; 4] },
37: }
38: 
39: /// Which routing layer decided the route
40: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
41: pub enum RoutingLayer {
42:     /// Layer 1 — direct peer in local cell
43:     Local,
44:     /// Layer 2 — via gateway in neighborhood
45:     Neighborhood,
46:     /// Layer 3 — via internet-connected global route
47:     Global,
48:     /// No route known — epidemic/opportunistic delivery
49:     StoreAndCarry,
50: }
51: 
52: /// Full routing decision with metadata
53: #[derive(Debug, Clone)]
54: pub struct RoutingDecision {
55:     /// Which message this route is for
56:     pub message_id: [u8; 16],
57:     /// The recipient we're trying to reach
58:     pub recipient_hint: [u8; 4],
59:     /// Primary path (where to try first)
60:     pub primary: NextHop,
61:     /// Alternative paths (for redundant delivery of high-priority messages)
62:     pub alternatives: Vec<NextHop>,
63:     /// Which layer provided the decision
64:     pub decided_by: RoutingLayer,
65:     /// Confidence in this route (0.0 - 1.0)
66:     pub confidence: f64,
67: }
68: 
69: /// Result of periodic maintenance tick

71: pub struct RoutingMaintenance {
72:     /// Peers moved from stale to active
73:     pub peers_promoted: usize,
74:     /// Peers moved from active to stale
75:     pub peers_demoted: usize,
76:     /// Stale gateways removed
77:     pub stale_gateways_removed: usize,
78:     /// Expired routes removed
79:     pub expired_routes_removed: usize,
80: }

1: /// CRDT Mesh Message Store for Drift Network
2: ///
3: /// A grow-only set (G-Set) CRDT implementation that guarantees
4: /// conflict-free merging in mesh networks where any two nodes
5: /// can meet and synchronize their message stores.
6: use std::collections::HashMap;
7: use std::sync::Arc;
8: 
9: /// Maximum messages in the store
10: const MAX_MESSAGES: usize = 10_000;
11: 
12: /// A unique message identifier (16 bytes, matches DriftEnvelope.message_id)
13: pub type MessageId = [u8; 16];
14: 
15: /// Stored envelope with metadata for routing/priority decisions
16: #[derive(Debug, Clone, serde::Serialize, serde::Deserialize)]
17: pub struct StoredEnvelope {
18:     /// Raw Drift Envelope bytes (serialized)
19:     pub envelope_data: Vec<u8>,
20:     /// Message ID (extracted for indexing)
21:     pub message_id: MessageId,
22:     /// Recipient hint (first 4 bytes of blake3(recipient_pk))
23:     pub recipient_hint: [u8; 4],
24:     /// When the message was created (unix timestamp u32)
25:     pub created_at: u32,
26:     /// TTL expiry (unix timestamp u32, 0 = never)
27:     pub ttl_expiry: u32,
28:     /// Number of relay hops this message has taken
29:     pub hop_count: u8,
30:     /// Message priority (0-255)
31:     pub priority: u8,
32:     /// When this node first received this message
33:     pub received_at: u64,
34: }
35: 
36: impl StoredEnvelope {
37:     /// Calculate priority score for sync ordering and eviction.
38:     ///
39:     /// Higher score = more important = synced first, evicted last.
40:     ///
41:     /// Factors:
42:     /// - priority: explicit priority field (0-255)
43:     /// - recency: newer messages score higher (exponential decay, τ = 24 hours)
44:     /// - hop_count: fewer hops = closer to origin = higher value
45:     /// - ttl_remaining: messages about to expire get priority
46:     pub fn priority_score(&self) -> f64 {
47:         let now = web_time::SystemTime::now()
48:             .duration_since(web_time::UNIX_EPOCH)
49:             .unwrap_or_default()
50:             .as_secs() as f64;
51: 
52:         let age_hours = (now - self.created_at as f64) / 3600.0;
53:         let recency = (-age_hours / 24.0).exp(); // τ = 24 hours
54: 
55:         let hop_penalty = 1.0 / (1.0 + self.hop_count as f64);
56: 
57:         let ttl_factor = if self.ttl_expiry == 0 {
58:             1.0 // No expiry = full score
59:         } else {
60:             let total_lifetime = (self.ttl_expiry as f64) - (self.created_at as f64);
61:             let remaining = (self.ttl_expiry as f64) - now;
62:             if total_lifetime <= 0.0 || remaining <= 0.0 {
63:                 0.0 // Expired
64:             } else {
65:                 (remaining / total_lifetime).clamp(0.0, 1.0)
66:             }
67:         };
68: 
69:         (self.priority as f64) * recency * hop_penalty * ttl_factor
70:     }
71: }

12: /// Result of a transport delivery attempt
13: struct TransportDeliveryResult {
14:     let transport: TransportType
15:     let success: Bool
16:     let latencyMs: UInt64
17:     let error: String?
18:     let timestamp: Date
19: }
20: 
21: /// Health metrics for a specific transport to a specific peer
22: struct TransportHealth: Codable {
23:     var lastSuccessAt: Date?
24:     var lastFailureAt: Date?
25:     var successCount: UInt64 = 0
26:     var failureCount: UInt64 = 0
27:     var averageLatencyMs: Double = 0
28:     var lastLatencyMs: UInt64 = 0
29:     
30:     /// Success rate (0.0 to 1.0)
31:     var successRate: Double {
32:         let total: UInt64 = successCount + failureCount
33:         guard total > 0 else { return 0.5 } // Unknown = neutral
34:         return Double(successCount) / Double(total)
35:     }
36:     
37:     /// Is this transport considered healthy?
38:     var isHealthy: Bool {
39:         // Healthy if success rate > 50% and not too many recent failures
40:         guard successRate > 0.5 else { return false }
41:         // If last failure was very recent (< 5s), be cautious
42:         if let lastFailure = lastFailureAt {
43:             return Date().timeIntervalSince(lastFailure) > 5.0
44:         }
45:         return true
46:     }
47:     
48:     /// Score for transport selection (higher = better)
49:     var score: Double {
50:         // Weight: 70% success rate, 30% latency (inverted, lower latency = higher score)
51:         let latencyScore: Double = averageLatencyMs > 0 ? min(1.0, 500.0 / averageLatencyMs) : 0.5
52:         return (successRate * 0.7) + (latencyScore * 0.3)
53:     }
54: }
55: 
56: /// Message deduplication entry
57: struct MessageDedupEntry {
58:     let messageId: String
59:     let firstReceivedAt: Date
60:     let firstTransport: TransportType
61:     var duplicateCount: UInt32 = 0
62:     var duplicateTimestamps: [Date] = []
63:     var duplicateTransports: [TransportType] = []
64: }

67: @MainActor
68: final class SmartTransportRouter {
69:     private let logger: Logger = Logger(subsystem: "com.scmessenger", category: "TransportRouter")

1: //! Backup encryption utilities using Argon2id / Blake3 and XChaCha20-Poly1305
2: //!
3: //! Encrypted identity backups use:
4: //! - Argon2id for key derivation on *user-facing* exports (memory-hard:
5: //!   resists GPU/ASIC brute force of weak human passphrases)
6: //! - Blake3 `derive_key` for *device-bound* auto-backups (the passphrase is
7: //!   a 256-bit random key stored in SharedPreferences — brute force is
8: //!   infeasible regardless of KDF cost, so sub-millisecond derivation is
9: //!   both safe and eliminates the 30-90s Argon2 stall on mobile)
10: //! - XChaCha20-Poly1305 for authenticated encryption (24-byte random nonce)
11: //! - Output format: hex(format_tag || salt || nonce || ciphertext_with_tag)
12: //!
13: //! Backups created with any prior format are still decryptable:
14: //! `decrypt_backup` tries Blake3 (0x03), Argon2id (0x02), then the older
15: //! PBKDF2-based formats. Every new *auto-backup* uses Blake3; every new
16: //! *user-facing export* uses Argon2id.
17: 
18: use crate::IronCoreError;
19: use argon2::{Algorithm, Argon2, Params, Version};
20: use chacha20poly1305::{
21:     aead::{Aead, KeyInit},
22:     XChaCha20Poly1305, XNonce,
23: };
24: use pbkdf2::pbkdf2_hmac;
25: use sha2::Sha256;
26: 
27: /// PBKDF2 iteration count. Retained only to decrypt backups created before
28: /// the switch to Argon2id — no longer used for new backups.
29: const PBKDF2_ITERATIONS: u32 = 600_000;
30: 
31: /// Format tag identifying an Argon2id-encrypted blob: `tag || salt || nonce
32: /// || ciphertext`. Older (untagged) blobs can't be confused with this format
33: /// in a way that would silently decrypt to the wrong plaintext — the AEAD
34: /// tag still has to authenticate correctly, so a coincidental first-byte
35: /// match just fails and `decrypt_backup` falls through to the older formats.
36: const FORMAT_TAG_ARGON2ID: u8 = 0x02;
37: 
38: /// Format tag for Blake3-derived key backups. Used for device-bound
39: /// auto-backups where the passphrase is a 256-bit random key (not a
40: /// human password). The Blake3 `derive_key` context disambiguates
41: /// this derivation from any other Blake3 usage in the crate.
42: const FORMAT_TAG_BLAKE3: u8 = 0x03;
43: 
44: /// Argon2id parameters, chosen per OWASP's password-storage minimums for
45: /// interactive login-class operations: 19 MiB memory, 2 iterations, 1
46: /// degree of parallelism. Embedding a format tag (rather than raw params)
47: /// means these can be tightened in a future format without breaking
48: /// decryption of blobs written today — a change would just get a new tag.
49: const ARGON2_MEMORY_KIB: u32 = 19 * 1024;
50: const ARGON2_TIME_COST: u32 = 2;
51: const ARGON2_PARALLELISM: u32 = 1;
52: 
53: /// Key length for XChaCha20-Poly1305 (256 bits = 32 bytes).
54: const KEY_LEN: usize = 32;
55: 
56: /// Nonce length for XChaCha20 (192 bits = 24 bytes).
57: const NONCE_LEN: usize = 24;
58: 
59: /// Tag length for Poly1305 (128 bits = 16 bytes).
60: const TAG_LEN: usize = 16;
61: 
62: /// Minimum encrypted data length (oldest, untagged format): nonce (24) + tag (16) = 40 bytes.
63: const MIN_DATA_LEN: usize = NONCE_LEN + TAG_LEN;
64: 
65: /// Derive a 32-byte key from a passphrase using Argon2id (memory-hard).
66: fn derive_key_argon2id(passphrase: &str, salt: &[u8]) -> Result<[u8; KEY_LEN], IronCoreError> {
67:     let params = Params::new(
68:         ARGON2_MEMORY_KIB,
69:         ARGON2_TIME_COST,
70:         ARGON2_PARALLELISM,
71:         Some(KEY_LEN),
72:     )
73:     .map_err(|_| IronCoreError::CryptoError)?;
74:     let argon2 = Argon2::new(Algorithm::Argon2id, Version::V0x13, params);
75: 
76:     let mut key = [0u8; KEY_LEN];
77:     argon2
78:         .hash_password_into(passphrase.as_bytes(), salt, &mut key)
79:         .map_err(|_| IronCoreError::CryptoError)?;
80:     Ok(key)

3: //! Provides immutable, cryptographically-linked audit trails for security-critical
4: //! operations. Each event is chained using Blake3 hashes to detect tampering.
5: //!
6: //! P0_SECURITY_005: Audit events are persisted to the storage backend and subject
7: //! to time-based retention (default: 365 days). Pruning preserves chain integrity
8: //! by keeping the oldest remaining event's prev_hash pointing to the pruned event's
9: //! hash, which is recorded in the `pruned_head_hash` field.

18: /// Type of audit event for categorization and policy enforcement

20: pub enum AuditEventType {
21:     /// New identity generated via `initialize_identity()`
22:     IdentityCreated,
23:     /// Identity explicitly deleted via backup deletion or factory reset
24:     IdentityDeleted,
25:     /// Encrypted message transmitted via `send_message()`
26:     MessageSent,
27:     /// Encrypted message received and successfully decrypted
28:     MessageReceived,
29:     /// Relay registration enabled via settings toggle
30:     RelayEnabled,
31:     /// Relay registration disabled via settings toggle  
32:     RelayDisabled,
33:     /// New contact added via QR scan or import
34:     ContactAdded,
35:     /// Contact explicitly blocked via block list
36:     ContactBlocked,
37:     /// Contact removed via explicit action
38:     ContactRemoved,
39:     /// Identity keys exported to platform backup
40:     BackupExported,
41:     /// Identity keys restored from platform backup
42:     BackupImported,
43:     /// Explicit consent granted for sensitive operation
44:     ConsentGranted,
45:     /// Storage compaction executed to reclaim space
46:     StorageCompacted,
47:     /// Static ECDH send used as fallback (legacy path)
48:     LegacyStaticEcdhSend,
49: }
50: 
51: impl fmt::Display for AuditEventType {
52:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {
53:         match self {
54:             AuditEventType::IdentityCreated => write!(f, "IdentityCreated"),
55:             AuditEventType::IdentityDeleted => write!(f, "IdentityDeleted"),
56:             AuditEventType::MessageSent => write!(f, "MessageSent"),
57:             AuditEventType::MessageReceived => write!(f, "MessageReceived"),
58:             AuditEventType::RelayEnabled => write!(f, "RelayEnabled"),
59:             AuditEventType::RelayDisabled => write!(f, "RelayDisabled"),
60:             AuditEventType::ContactAdded => write!(f, "ContactAdded"),
61:             AuditEventType::ContactBlocked => write!(f, "ContactBlocked"),
62:             AuditEventType::ContactRemoved => write!(f, "ContactRemoved"),
63:             AuditEventType::BackupExported => write!(f, "BackupExported"),
64:             AuditEventType::BackupImported => write!(f, "BackupImported"),
65:             AuditEventType::ConsentGranted => write!(f, "ConsentGranted"),
66:             AuditEventType::StorageCompacted => write!(f, "StorageCompacted"),
67:             AuditEventType::LegacyStaticEcdhSend => write!(f, "LegacyStaticEcdhSend"),
68:         }
69:     }
70: }

2: 
3: use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
4: 
5: /// What kind of message this is
6: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
7: pub enum MessageType {
8:     /// Plain text message
9:     Text,
10:     /// Delivery/read receipt
11:     Receipt,
12:     /// Onion relay packet (internal use for forwarding)
13:     OnionRelay,
14: }
15: 
16: /// Delivery status of a message
17: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
18: pub enum DeliveryStatus {
19:     /// Message sent (left this device)
20:     Sent,
21:     /// Message delivered to recipient's device
22:     Delivered,
23:     /// Deprecated: retained for backward-compatible deserialization of receipts
24:     /// from older peers. Treated as no-op (mapped to `Delivered` in processing).
25:     /// Do not emit — Zero-Status Architecture: read receipts are no longer
26:     /// emitted or displayed. (Not `#[deprecated]` because the UniFFI scaffolding
27:     /// must construct it, and generated code cannot carry allow attributes.)
28:     Read,
29:     /// Delivery failed
30:     Failed,
31: }
32: 
33: /// A plaintext message before encryption.
34: ///
35: /// This is what the application layer creates. It gets encrypted into
36: /// an `Envelope` before hitting the wire.
37: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
38: pub struct Message {
39:     /// Unique message ID (UUID v4)
40:     pub id: String,
41:     /// Sender's identity ID (Blake3 hash of Ed25519 public key)
42:     pub sender_id: String,
43:     /// Recipient's identity ID
44:     pub recipient_id: String,
45:     /// Message type
46:     pub message_type: MessageType,
47:     /// Payload bytes (UTF-8 text for Text messages, serialized Receipt for receipts)
48:     pub payload: Vec<u8>,
49:     /// Unix timestamp (seconds)
50:     pub timestamp: u64,
51: }
52: 
53: /// A delivery receipt
54: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
55: pub struct Receipt {
56:     /// ID of the message this receipt is for
57:     pub message_id: String,
58:     /// New delivery status
59:     pub status: DeliveryStatus,
60:     /// Unix timestamp of the status change
61:     pub timestamp: u64,
62: }
63: 
64: /// An encrypted message envelope — what actually goes on the wire.
65: ///
66: /// Contains everything a recipient needs to decrypt the message,
67: /// assuming they have their own private key.
68: ///
69: /// When `ratchet_dh_public` is present, the envelope was encrypted using
70: /// the Double Ratchet protocol (forward secrecy). The `ephemeral_public_key`
71: /// field carries the ratchet DH public key instead of a per-message ECDH key,
72: /// and `ratchet_message_number` identifies the chain position.
73: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
